newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israel's Levy meets Mubarak to improve ties.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Levy meets Mubarak to improve ties.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Thursday met Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy in Cairo to try to improve the atmosphere between the two states.
Mubarak and Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa will also brief Levy on the president's recent talks with Syrian leader Hafez al-Assad in Damascus, officials said.
"I am going first to improve the atmosphere and to brief and be briefed," Levy told Israel Radio earlier on Thursday.
Israel Radio said Levy will also try to ensure that next week's Middle East economic conference in Cairo does not turn into an Israel-bashing session.

"I was invited a month ago officially to participate in the Cairo conference. Israel will participate, it has an interest," Levy told the radio, adding that he hoped the meeting would not "be exploited for political head butting".

Israel's agriculture and infrastructure ministries said this week they would not send official delegations to the economic conference but Agriculture Minister Raphael Eitan said on Thursday he had decided to send a delegation because things had improved.
Israel's Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon had said no one from his ministry would attend the summit because Egypt's political leaders and newspapers had been attacking the Israeli government.

Egypt, the Palestinians, and other Arab states have become frustrated with the near standstill in peace moves since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won Israel's May elections, ousting a centre-left government that had conducted negotiations on the principle of trading occupied Arab land for peace.

Netanyahu opposes trading land for peace. His government is locked in talks with the PLO on implementing a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron signed by the previous government.
